title: Personal Assistant That Remembers You
subtitle: Design a memory layer that recalls each user's preferences and past tasks within 300 ms, keeps users apart and forgets on request.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Promises and constraints
practice_prompts.hint: Name the four promises, the 300 ms question and what must never be stored.

practice_prompts.label: Scopes, keys and the turn
practice_prompts.hint: Give each scope its key, write rule and lifetime, then trace one turn through read, reply and write.

practice_prompts.label: Bounds, isolation and failures
practice_prompts.hint: Bound prompt and storage separately, say where user_id comes from, and name how the design breaks.

practice_prompts.label: Proof and cost
practice_prompts.hint: Describe the recall harness and answer the cost pivot.

rubric: Separates thread-scoped memory from user-scoped long-term memory and names the key for each scope.
Gives semantic facts stable keys with one prior version and episodes fresh keys with a cap and digest.
Names an embedding index filtered by user for episodes, and key reads for facts.
Shows the read path fits in 300 ms p95 in parallel and moves every write after the reply.
Takes user_id from auth only and makes forget and account deletion reach every store, index and cache.
Says what is not persisted and how a contradicting preference is handled.
Proves recall with planted facts across turns and conversations, plus false-memory and cross-user tests.

editorial_review.evidence: Compared all 28 captured sections against the earlier draft paragraph by paragraph. The draft had dropped the verbatim prompt, the three architecture boundaries, 'short-term is scope not lifetime', MemGPT and extractor-on-queue, the 10-vs-10,000 demo point, 'budget memory like any dependency', the hidden-context cost paragraph, FDE line and four verbs, the seven round-carrying lines and the source's two-minute answer (replaced by a paraphrase); all are restored. It gave all three section-4 diagrams one identical caption; each now has a caption and walkthrough matching its labels, with the 'whole system' pair before the control-plane bullets and the three-lane drawing after, as in the source. Check-yourself answers were reworded and follow-ups were a table: all 12 checks and 8 follow-ups are now reveals that start from the source answer, plus the cost pivot and one labelled authored drill (22 total). Restating paragraphs under the failure table and in the brief were replaced with explanation (latency longest-chain arithmetic, where each failure is observable, sizing chain). A scrubbed em dash had left a ', ' table cell and broken the verbatim rubric line; both fixed. Authored additions (illustrative trace, deletion marker, task identity, 400 GB overhead caveat) are labelled.
